project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child shows a small book with a drawing of a face and of the body, names five parts of the body, shows how to brush the teeth and recites a short rhyme.

activities.goal_en: Listen to a rhyme, say it with gestures and name parts of the body.
activities.prompt_en: Listen and do the actions with me.
steps_en: Say the rhyme slowly once, with the gestures.
Say it again; the child does the gestures.
Say it together, line by line.
Ask: which parts of the body are in the rhyme?
observe_en: Does the gestures at the right time.
Says some words of the rhyme.
Names the body parts of the rhyme.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 15 (Poetry and Rhymes: Rhymes), p. 40; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en:
Two little hands go clap, clap, clap,
Two little feet go tap, tap, tap,
Two little eyes can see, see, see,
One little nose, and that is me!

activities.goal_en: Show moods with facial expressions and recognise them on others.
activities.prompt_en: Show me a happy face! Now a sad face. Now a surprised face!
steps_en: Show a happy face and say “happy”.
Show a sad face and say “sad”.
The child copies each face.
Show a face without speaking; the child says the mood.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 16 (Sign Language and Gestures: Facial expressions), p. 41; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Draw horizontal lines from left to right.
activities.prompt_en: Draw a road for the little car: from the left to the right!
steps_en: Show the left hand and the right hand.
Draw a line in the air from left to right.
Move a toy car along a line on the floor from left to right.
Draw roads on paper from left to right.
observe_en: Draws a line without lifting the crayon.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 18 (Writing: Pre-letter formation), p. 43; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.prompt_en: In French, we say our name like this: “Je m’appelle Ngum.” Now you!
steps_en: Point to yourself and say “Je m’appelle…” with your name.
The child repeats with their own name.
Pass a ball: whoever catches it says “Je m’appelle…”.
Ask a puppet: “Comment tu t’appelles ?”
source_refs: Nursery One, table 19 (French: Se présenter), p. 44; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Count fingers up to 5 and show a number with the fingers.
activities.prompt_en: How many fingers are on one hand? Let us count them together.
steps_en: Show one hand and count each finger, touching it.
The child counts their own fingers.
Say a number from 1 to 5; the child shows that many fingers.
Count eyes, ears and noses too.
observe_en: Counts up to 5 touching each finger.
Shows a number with the fingers.
Says how many eyes and ears we have.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Counting), p. 45; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: How many fingers are on one hand?
interactive.explanation_en: Count with me: one, two, three, four, five. There are 5 fingers on one hand.

activities.title_en: Hot or cold, soft or hard?
activities.goal_en: Touch objects and say if they are hot or cold, soft or hard, dry or wet.
activities.prompt_en: Close your eyes and touch. Is it soft or hard? Is it wet or dry?
steps_en: Prepare safe objects: cotton, a stone, a wet cloth, a dry cloth, a cup of cool water.
The child touches one object at a time.
Ask: soft or hard? wet or dry?
Put the objects into two groups.
materials_en: a wet cloth and a dry cloth
source_refs: Nursery One, table 21 (Sensory and Perceptive Education: The sense of touch), p. 46; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Distinguish sweet and bitter tastes and know that medicine is taken only from an adult.
activities.prompt_en: Taste a little. Is it sweet like sugar or bitter like bitter leaf?
steps_en: Give a tiny taste of sugar water.
Give a tiny taste of cooked bitter leaf.
Ask: sweet or bitter?
Explain: medicine is only given by a parent or a nurse.
observe_en: Tastes only what the adult gives.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 21 (Sensory and Perceptive Education: The sense of taste), p. 46; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

activities.goal_en: Brush the teeth correctly, morning and evening.
activities.prompt_en: We brush our teeth in the morning and before going to bed: up and down, front and back.
steps_en: Show a toothbrush with a little toothpaste.
Brush the teeth of a doll or a drawing: up and down.
The child brushes their own teeth with you.
Rinse the mouth with clean water.
observe_en: Brushes the front and the back teeth.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 28 (Health Education and Nutrition: Good health habits), p. 54; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Use the polite words please, thank you, sorry and excuse me.
activities.prompt_en: When we ask, we say “please”. When we receive, we say “thank you”. When we hurt someone, we say “sorry”.
steps_en: Act with a puppet: it asks for a crayon without “please”.
Ask: what word is missing?
Practise the three words in small scenes.
Praise each polite word used during the day.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 25 (Character Education: Simple etiquettes), p. 51; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Clothes for the sun and the rain
activities.goal_en: Choose clothes that protect the body in hot, cold or rainy weather.
activities.prompt_en: Look outside. Is it sunny or rainy? What should we wear today?
steps_en: Show clothes: a cap, a raincoat, a pullover, a tee shirt.
Show a picture of the sun; the child chooses clothes.
Show a picture of the rain; the child chooses again.
Ask: what do you wear when it is cold?
observe_en: Chooses light clothes for the sun.
Chooses a raincoat or umbrella for the rain.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 26 (Environmental Education: Climate change), p. 52; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

activities.goal_en: Draw a circle and turn it into a face.
activities.prompt_en: Draw a big round circle. Now add two eyes, a nose and a mouth!
steps_en: Draw a circle in the air with the finger.
Draw a big circle on paper.
Add two eyes, a nose and a smiling mouth.
Colour the face and add hair.
observe_en: Places eyes, nose and mouth inside.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 30 (Drawing and Colouring: Shapes and colouring), p. 56; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Touch your head, touch your knees
activities.goal_en: Locate parts of the body and move them on a signal.
activities.prompt_en: Touch your head! Touch your knees! Touch your toes! Stand up tall!
steps_en: Name a part of the body and touch it.
The child copies quickly.
Go faster, then slower.
Finish by stretching up high and breathing slowly.
observe_en: Touches the right part of the body.
Stretches and breathes calmly at the end.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 32 (Physical Education and Sports: Athletics), p. 58; theme 2: The body (table 13, p. 37)

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Names at least five parts of the body.
Counts fingers up to 5 on one hand.
Shows happy and sad with the face.
Says hot, cold, soft, hard when touching.
Shows how to brush the teeth.
Draws a face with a circle.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery One tables, cited and not reproduced.
